title: Problem Overview
content:
**Erdős Problem #764** asks: can the 3-fold convolution sum ∑ 1_A * 1_A * 1_A be cN + O(1)?

**Answer: NO** (Vaughan 1972). Even the weaker bound cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}) is impossible.

This generalizes the Erdős-Fuchs theorem (1956) for 2-fold convolutions. The result applies to any h-fold convolution with h ≥ 2.

title: Convolution Definitions
content:
**conv2 A n:** 2-fold convolution counting #{(a,b) ∈ A² : a + b = n}.

**conv3 A n:** 3-fold convolution counting #{(a,b,c) ∈ A³ : a + b + c = n}.

**convH h A n (axiom):** General h-fold convolution, axiomatized because the definition requires dependent types.

**sumConv2, sumConv3:** Cumulative sums ∑_{n≤N} conv(A, n), the quantities whose growth rate is studied.

title: Error Bound Hierarchy
content:
**IsLinearBounded f c:** f(N) = cN + O(1), bounded error. This is what Erdős asked about.

**IsLinearLittleO f c α:** f(N) = cN + o(N^α), error grows slower than N^α.

**IsLinearVaughan f c:** f(N) = cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}), the precise bound Vaughan proved impossible.

The hierarchy: IsLinearBounded ⟹ IsLinearVaughan ⟹ IsLinearLittleO (for α = 1/4).

title: Erdős-Fuchs Theorem (2-fold case)
content:
**erdos_fuchs_theorem (axiom):** No set A has ∑ 1_A * 1_A = cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}). The foundational 1956 result.

**erdos_fuchs_corollary (axiom):** No set A has ∑ 1_A * 1_A = cN + O(1). Since bounded error implies the weaker bound, this follows.

title: Vaughan's Theorem (3-fold and h-fold)
content:
**vaughan_3fold_theorem (axiom):** No set A has ∑ 1_A * 1_A * 1_A = cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}). The strong form.

**vaughan_corollary (axiom):** No set A has ∑ 1_A * 1_A * 1_A = cN + O(1). The direct answer to Problem #764: NO.

**vaughan_hfold_theorem (axiom):** Applies to any h-fold convolution with h ≥ 2. Completely general.

title: Error Oscillation
content:
**ErrorOscillates f c:** The error f(N) - cN is infinitely often above N^{1/4} and infinitely often below -N^{1/4}. It cannot stay bounded on one side.

**error_oscillation (axiom):** For any infinite set A, the 3-fold convolution error must oscillate by at least N^{1/4} infinitely often.

title: Squares Example
content:
**squares_not_linear (proved):** Even for A = {0, 1, 4, 9, 16, ...} (perfect squares), the 3-fold sum cannot be cN + O(1).

Proved directly from vaughan_corollary. Waring's problem studies the same convolution but without requiring linear growth.

title: Montgomery-Vaughan Refinement and Tightness
content:
**montgomery_vaughan_refinement (axiom):** Even o(N^{1/4}) is impossible (removing the log factor from Erdős-Fuchs).

**quarter_exponent_tight (axiom):** There exist sets where the error is O(N^{α}) for any α > 1/4. The 1/4 exponent is essentially best possible — it cannot be improved.

title: Summary Theorem
content:
**erdos_764_summary (proved from axioms):**

Combines three impossibility results:
1. 3-fold sum cannot be cN + O(1) (vaughan_corollary)
2. Cannot even be cN + o(N^{1/4}/(log N)^{1/2}) (vaughan_3fold_theorem)
3. Generalizes to h-fold for all h ≥ 2 (vaughan_hfold_theorem)

Proved by: `⟨vaughan_corollary, vaughan_3fold_theorem, vaughan_hfold_theorem⟩`
